answer: Resist sybils by requiring every new identity to lock a deposit drawn from a shared ocean of escrow, equal to the prior epoch's median spendable and held until two closes after its first accepted answer. Peers enforce this at the eligibility summit: before attesting or assigning a grading seat, they verify the deposit receipt and reject any reused or missing bond. A colliding deposit hash is slashed by a majority of established attestors, so cloning identities costs real locked capital, not just another login. The compact sonnet of the rule is one hash, checked on every countersignature.
